title: Unified discount guardrails and quoting exception process
creator: Maya Patel
description: Define a single source of truth for allowable discount tiers, approval flows for exceptions, and the operational steps to keep SFDC pricebook, internal quoting tools, and the Security Questionnaire (SSQ) answers in sync. This ticket covers policy, an experiment to validate narrower guardrails, and an ops runbook for exception handling so Sales can quote enterprise deals quickly without bypassing procurement or legal controls.
background: Recent enterprise deals have shown inconsistent discounting decisions across regions and reps; pricing deviations are being tracked in ad-hoc spreadsheets. Security questionnaire answers occasionally reference pricing commitments that are not reflected in the official pricebook, causing legal review delays. We need standardized guardrails that reduce cycle time for deal closure while protecting margin and ensuring compliance with SSQs.
objectives: Create clear discount bands by customer tier and ARR that map to approval requirements
Define a two-step exception approval path (Sales Ops -> Revenue Ops -> VP Sales signoff) with SLA
Update SFDC pricebook and quoting templates to reflect approved tiers and escalation flags
Publish an SSQ alignment checklist so legal/security answers reflect only approved pricing language
Run a 6-week experiment narrowing discount windows for new inbound leads and measure impact on win rate and time-to-sign
acceptance_criteria: Discount bands documented and approved by Finance and RevOps
Updated pricebook uploaded to SFDC and referenced in at least two quoting templates
Exception approval playbook published in Confluence with contact roster and SLA
SSQ answer set updated and versioned; Legal confirms no blocking language
Experiment monitoring dashboard (win rate, TTS, average ACV, discount burn) live in Looker

2025-02-27: Drafted proposed bands (Standard: 0-10%, Manager Approval 10-20%, Executive Approval 20-35%); flagged EMEA distribution anomalies
2025-03-01: Sales leadership requested pilot in NA only for 6 weeks; Legal requested SSQ template sample prior to rollout
2025-03-03: RevOps agreed to a temporary validation rule in SFDC to tag quotes using deprecated SKUs; Engineering asked to prioritize automation ticket to sync pricebook (ENG-20412)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Narrowing discount windows may slow enterprise close rates — Mitigation: 6-week A/B pilot and daily gating to revert if TTS increases >15%
Risk: Sales bypassing process for large deals — Mitigation: require Salesforce field and automated alerts to Revenue Ops when a quote uses discount > Manager approval
Risk: SSQ/pricebook drift — Mitigation: monthly reconciliation job and a named owner in Legal/RevOps
plan_and_milestones: Week 1: Finalize bands, secure Finance/Legal signoff
Week 2: Implement SFDC pricebook changes and validation flags; update quote templates
Week 3: Publish SSQ alignment checklist; train Sales Ops and AEs (30-min sync)
Week 4-9: Run NA pilot experiment; monitor dashboard daily
Week 10: Review pilot results and decide full rollout or iterate
